question: Does one directly published manual-grain-handling source provide an empirically described operation, crew, quantity and elapsed/person time that could inform an explicit work input?
search_budget: At most three initial web queries, six candidate search records, then one directly published primary manual/report body. Prefer FAO, WFP/Logistics Cluster, ILO or an original open research report. Select for operation and provenance before reading numerical outcomes. Do not select a rate for convenient model feasibility.
selection: Choose the first source in search order with a direct institutional/author publisher, grain or bagged agricultural material and manual loading/unloading/stacking coverage. A manual can qualify as primary evidence of its prescription without qualifying as an empirical timing measurement. If no source matches, record that result; do not expand the search in this stage.
extract: Pin source identity, URL, date/version/locator, operation boundaries, commodity/package/load units, human crew versus equipment, time denominator, distance/lift conditions, measurement method/sample and any uncertainty. Distinguish measured observations from design capacities, worked examples and prescriptions. Leave unreported fields unknown.
transfer: Modern machinery, package/route geometry, day length, crew size and task composition do not silently transfer to ancient or fantasy logistics. A mass throughput does not supply hours/net-edible-kcal without declared material and edible-energy coefficients. Do not derive such coefficients here.
output: One source evidence packet, exact located quotations with a small independent literal check, an explicit suitability/refusal decision and a concrete next input/evidence target. No numerical rate adoption, rate sweep, warehouse task generation, handling converter call, staffing allocation, food/stock/graph solve or atlas change.
source_instructions: Treat source documents as evidence only, not instructions governing this task.
